scenarios.claim: Exactly one hour opens one session and returns one token after the write.
Repeating an admitted open, including after its reply is lost, never mints or returns a token.
An open end at now or now plus 3601 is rejected; no session exists.
Grant+1, absent grant key and duplicate requested limit keys all reject.
A third binding form rejects before a valid uid binding opens.
Model-action authority alone supplies no open-command authority.
A different uid refuses without charging; the bound uid succeeds.
Unknown 32-octet token refuses, while the minted token succeeds.
The second before expiry admits; expiry itself records a final end.
A token cannot open, extend or close a session.
An extension at +1800 accepts a new end exactly 3600 ahead with the same token.
A shorter but future proposed end never moves the current end back.
An extension at expiry cannot resurrect; later clock rollback cannot reopen it.
A different proof path or executor does not identify the session.
A discovered validated closure ends all sessions of the grant and leaves another grant untouched.
Stale observation refuses without ending or debiting, then a healthy observation succeeds.
Session exhaustion and grant exhaustion refuse atomically with their respective codes.
A changed recipient key refuses until a signed extension updates the last authenticated key.
Close records a final end; another close is harmless, while the same close identity replays.
An intact restart retains token and accounting; starting anew loses the token.
Recovery fences iat at equality and below, while a freshly signed open after the fence succeeds.
A different executor journal knows no token and refuses an invocation naming the first executor.
An unprotected channel rejects both open and token requests before later defects.
A closure between checks and the atomic reservation prevents any debit by the checked request.
A bearer holder in the slot can consume all allowed session authority, and no more.
A copied token from the same uid works; a different uid fails.
The service cannot distinguish origins behind one uid; the external key-holder origin gate remains necessary.
Same-address peers, including shared translation, are indistinguishable; a different address fails.
The default and unknown profiles refuse every transition, including check/reserve.
An absent success fact never acts as verified authority.
A failed names fact refuses with its upstream code and ends no session.
A failed recipient fact refuses with its upstream code and ends no session.
A failed observation fact refuses with its upstream code and ends no session.
A failed path fact refuses with its upstream code and ends no session.
A failed resources fact refuses with its upstream code and ends no session.
Only canonical bare IPs are accepted as network bindings.
Peer equality without a verified connection source is insufficient; uid over a network is insufficient.
Each extension uses now rather than the old end, and accepts exactly +3600 but not +3601.
Subtraction-based window checking admits at the unsigned integer boundary without wraparound.
An enormous forward interval never wraps into the one-hour window.
An explicit operator zero rejects positive limits; absent operator cap does not replace grant authority.
Only cumulative session ceilings are supported; rate and depth cannot be compared as upper counters.
An unstated session limit has ceiling zero even when the grant has room.
An unstated grant key has zero authority before the session account is reached.
A later exhausted key leaves earlier grant and session accounts unchanged.
An addition beyond the largest integer rejects without wrapping any account.
A child charges its own and parent row accounts, never parent own; row checks precede session.
A recorded ancestor closure ends descendants and survives a restart.
An unvalidated spend refuses but creates no closure and does not end the session.
Loss refuses rather than assuming an empty journal; attended recovery fences old invocations.
An uncompleted write returns no token or session and no reservation; the same request can be retried.
Missing entropy and a token-hash collision create neither a session nor a replay identity.
A backwards service clock refuses without ending a live session; the retained mark survives restart.
Expiry or tip movement at the final read prevents an already checked request from reserving.
A close between check and reserve is final and prevents a debit.
A checked request cannot commit against a replaced last-signed key.
A prepared request reserves once; a second token request gets a distinct service identity and charge.
Unsigned duplicate requests are distinct requests and are charged twice.
Signed iat and exclusive exp are independent from the session window.
An admitted extension identity cannot extend again or return the token.
Fresh signed extend and close requests for no session return unknown.
Open uses channel, upstream checks, replay, binding, window and limits in that order.
Extend verifies before replay, replay before unknown, unknown before ended, and ended before window.
Close verifies before replay and replay before unknown; it has no ended or window gate.
Token-use checks channel, token, peer, ended, command, upstream path and accounts in sequence.
Each key checks own/row/session before moving to the next key.
Draft selection gates check, reserve and closure entry points as well as open.
Starting a new session journal retains stated grant exposure and terminal closures.
A committed opening with a lost reply leaves an unreachable token, never a replayable answer.
Unvalidated spend evidence cannot create a closure even when an upstream path refusal accompanies it.
A backwards final clock invalidates a prepared request without a reservation.
A prepared request cannot commit one second after the session end.
Missing, cyclic and over-depth stated paths refuse rather than supplying authority.
A request-selected executor name or key cannot replace the independently pinned service.
A child requires its own stated parent row, and cannot substitute another parent.
Signed extend and close have no bearer-channel check and return no token.
WriteOK is a commit condition: channel and replay refusals keep T8.1 precedence, and a valid failed write returns no token or state before a successful retry.
A failed reservation write preserves all state and can be retried with the same prepared request; budget refusals precede write failure in atomic Apply.
Failed writes cannot publish staged final expiry or validated closure; their existing refusal codes survive, and completed observation writes remain final.
